observations.summary: The chat-list contract fixes overscan, stable identity, hot-memory caps, skeleton loading, message jumping, search highlighting, and tail-follow behavior.
Auditor settings resolve and persist a provider/model pair from an account-bound registry and freeze the selected pair at sweep start for reporting.
Persona behavior includes manual, auto, and hybrid modes, natural-language invocation, scoped overrides, eligibility restrictions, and lock controls.

The inline visualizer is an allow-scripts sandbox whose postMessage bridge can enqueue prompts, open links, copy text, and request resizing; the prose also declares sanitizer and external-network restrictions.
Natural-language mode invocation records requested/effective fields and closes the overlay enums while preserving deep_plan history.

candidate_findings.title: Visible-slice loads have no stale-completion contract
candidate_findings.claim: The capsule specifies index-based asynchronous replacement of skeletons and asynchronous ID-to-index loading, but it does not bind a load to an immutable thread, window generation, or stable-ID set, nor define cancellation or apply-if-current behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Rapid scrolling, thread switching, retry, rewind, or concurrent insertion can let an older completion populate a newer index/window, displaying the wrong message and potentially crossing thread boundaries.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define request identity and generation fields, immutable thread/message binding, cancellation semantics, apply-if-current checks, idempotent retry, and stale-success/stale-error discard rules.

candidate_findings.title: Performance goals lack a certifiable oracle
candidate_findings.claim: The contract fixes overscan at 10 and admits that 10k-plus threads may require pagination, but gives no target hardware, frame-time budget, scroll velocity, load latency, peak memory, or pass/fail workload.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can satisfy the structural prose while still janking, blanking during fast scroll, or exhausting memory; tuning can also change behavior without a regression gate.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify representative thread shapes and content sizes, target device classes, p50/p95 slice-load latency, frame and memory budgets, fast-scroll behavior, and deterministic benchmarks that decide when load-older becomes mandatory.

candidate_findings.title: Search-highlight cache omits content revision and offset units
candidate_findings.claim: Highlight ranges are cached only by message_id and query; the capsule does not key them by content revision or define whether offsets are bytes, Unicode scalar values, UTF-16 units, or grapheme clusters.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Streaming, edits, rewinds, normalization, or emoji/multibyte text can make cached ranges point at incorrect text or invalid boundaries.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the offset coordinate system, cache key including immutable content revision/hash, invalidation on every content mutation, and tests covering streaming edits, normalization, emoji, combining marks, and rewind.

candidate_findings.title: Stored Auditor provider value has no explicit account identity semantics
candidate_findings.claim: The dropdown is account-bound, but the normative persisted pair is only provider and model; this capsule does not say whether provider is an immutable provider-entry/account ID, a provider kind, or a display name.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: With multiple accounts for one provider, credential rotation, rename, or registry reorder, the same stored values can resolve to a different credential boundary and produce audit evidence under the wrong account.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define an immutable account-bound provider-entry identifier, requested/effective account identity, rename/deletion migration, credential-boundary checks, and the exact identity fields included in the sweep-start snapshot and report.

candidate_findings.title: First-eligible fallback has no stable ordering or tie-breaker
candidate_findings.claim: Fallback chooses the first eligible provider entry and model while also claiming no environment-dependent branching, but this capsule defines neither canonical ordering nor a registry snapshot/tie-break rule.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Discovery timing, cache order, account insertion order, or concurrent readiness changes can select different Auditor runtimes from the same logical settings, invalidating reproducibility.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define stable provider-entry and model ordering, tie-break keys, the registry/version snapshot used for resolution, behavior during concurrent registry changes, and a terminal outcome when no eligible pair exists.

candidate_findings.title: Auditor fallback covers unavailable provider but not the rest of the failure state space
candidate_findings.claim: The acceptance criteria define fallback for an unavailable saved provider only; no behavior is defined here for a missing model, revoked credentials, capability/policy rejection, readiness timeout, registry failure, or zero eligible pairs.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A mandatory audit loop can hang, silently remap, repeatedly fail, or emit misleading provider/model evidence when common runtime failures occur.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define failure-state taxonomy, requested/effective pair disclosure, retry and timeout policy, fallback-loop prevention, cancellation and recovery behavior, warning persistence, and the explicit critically-blocked result when no eligible runtime exists.

candidate_findings.title: Natural-language child-run creation lacks an authority gate contract
candidate_findings.claim: Requests including Run that with Bash can create or route a child run whenever the surrounding task permits delegation, but the caller, permission evaluator, inherited sandbox posture, confirmation rule, and denial path are not defined in this capsule.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Ambiguous natural language could trigger code execution or delegated repository access with broader permissions, secrets, or side effects than the user intended.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Name the authority owner and caller, define capability and permission checks before creation, sandbox/secret inheritance, confirmation thresholds for side-effecting personas, denial copy, cancellation, and an auditable provenance record tying the child run to the user utterance.

candidate_findings.title: Persona override and lock behavior has no complete state machine
candidate_findings.claim: Hybrid mode permits temporary or persistent overrides, phrases map to turn or session scope, and the UI can lock/unlock, but precedence and transitions among mode, lock, override scope, auto resolution, thread change, restart, Persona deletion, and run-in-progress are unspecified.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The effective Persona and visible badge can diverge, a supposedly temporary override can persist, or an in-flight run can change identity mid-execution.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define authoritative state fields, precedence table, transition events, scope expiration boundaries, persistence rules, sweep/run snapshot timing, unlock/reset behavior, deleted-Persona recovery, and deterministic transition tests.

candidate_findings.title: Retired Persona aliases remain in an unqualified Rules list
candidate_findings.claim: The prose says assistant-local _id substitutes normalize to canonical names, then lists requested_persona_id and effective_persona_id under Rules without marking them input-only aliases, forbidden output fields, or migration-only names.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementers can serialize both schemas, expose retired fields in GUI/runtime snapshots, or disagree about which value wins when canonical and legacy fields conflict.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Publish one normative field schema and a migration table defining accepted legacy inputs, canonical outputs, conflict precedence, telemetry for legacy use, persistence rewrite, and removal version.

candidate_findings.title: Privileged postMessage bridge lacks caller authentication and per-method policy
candidate_findings.claim: The only bridge is postMessage and it exposes prompt queueing, external-link opening, clipboard writes, and resizing, but this capsule does not require event.source/frame-instance validation, a capability nonce, strict message schemas, payload/rate limits, user-gesture checks, URL-scheme policy, or teardown revocation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A stale, sibling, compromised, or malicious visual frame could invoke host capabilities, enqueue content into the wrong thread/questionnaire, open unsafe protocols, spam UI operations, or retain authority after unmount.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Require frame-instance capability tokens, event.source binding, schema/version validation, origin handling for opaque sandbox origins, lifecycle revocation, method-specific size/rate limits, user activation for sensitive calls, URL normalization and scheme allowlists, and audited denial responses.

candidate_findings.title: Network-denial and sanitizer policy lack enforceable closure
candidate_findings.claim: The capsule permits scripts, declares arbitrary external network loads denied, and describes a DOMPurify default safe subset plus approved URL-bearing attributes, but does not name the enforcement layer or enumerate sanitizer version/configuration, URL attributes, protocols, SVG rules, CSS handling, CSP, or egress test cases.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Sandbox allow-scripts alone does not prevent outbound requests, and an underspecified sanitizer/URL policy can enable exfiltration, unsafe navigation, parser differentials, or version-dependent behavior.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Lock an exact sanitizer version/config and tag/attribute/protocol matrix; define CSP or host-level egress enforcement for fetch, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, media, fonts, images, imports, workers, DNS/navigation channels, and supply adversarial fixtures proving denial.

candidate_findings.title: Mode invocation fields lack defaults, closed metadata enums, and transition rules
candidate_findings.claim: The capsule requires selection_source, selection_reason, and override_scope alongside requested/effective mode fields, but closes only the overlay and runtime-mode enums and provides no defaults, nullability, precedence, scope lifetime, or invalid-combination behavior for the metadata fields.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Resolvers and GUI projections can produce incompatible records or different effective modes for the same utterance, and tests cannot distinguish a valid unresolved/default state from missing data.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define field types, closed enums, defaults/nullability, owner and writer, precedence between explicit controls and natural language, transition and expiration rules, persistence/migration behavior, invalid-combination handling, and deterministic input-to-record fixtures.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Virtualized items have stable IDs, and streaming auto-scroll explicitly stops when the user has scrolled up.
Skeleton-load failure has an error placeholder and Retry, and missing or rewound jump targets have a Message not found state.
Auditor setting changes are explicitly deferred to the next sweep, and reports must mirror the provider/model resolved at sweep start.
Direct-chat Persona eligibility is explicit, and unresolved natural-language or persisted Persona references have visible clarification or fallback behavior.
The visualizer policy explicitly denies same-origin, forms, popups, top navigation, and arbitrary external network loads, even though enforcement details are missing.
deep_plan is explicitly preserved through normalization and historical/runtime records.

exact_evidence_refs.excerpt: Only the **visible viewport** plus an **overscan of 10 items** above and below should be rendered at any time. Config: `ui.chat.virtualization_overscan`, default `10`. Tune based on Slint rendering performance.
Each message or block (user message, assistant message, diff block, thought stream, subagent block, etc.) must have a **stable ID** (e.g. message_id or event_id).

**Skeleton placeholders (24.4.1) -- full spec (MVP):** (1) **Purpose:** During thread load or fast scroll, show skeleton placeholders for not-yet-loaded items so the list does not pop or show blanks. (2) **When:** Thread load = **8 skeleton rows** until first slice is loaded (Config: `ui.chat.skeleton_row_count`, default `8`); scroll = skeletons for new visible window until slice content is ready, then replace in place. (3) **UI:** Simple grey rounded bars (one or two lines; optional different heights for user/assistant/diff); theme-aware; replace in place when content arrives to avoid jump/flicker. (4) **Data:** UI-only; for any visible index without content, render skeleton; when slice loader returns data, re-render. (5) **Slint:** Reusable skeleton component; list model signals loading per index. (6) **Edge cases:** On load failure, show error placeholder + Retry; do not leave skeletons indefinitely.

**Jump to message (24.4.2) -- full spec (MVP):** (1) **Purpose:** Jump to a message from search results (§10), shared link, or command palette; virtual list scrolls to target and optionally highlights it. (2) **When:** Search result "Go to message"; URL/deep link to message; optional "Go to message..." command. (3) **UI:** Scroll so target (by stable ID or index) is in viewport (centered or upper third); ensure slice containing target is loaded (target_index ± overscan); optional brief highlight or focus, fading after a few seconds. (4) **Data:** Resolve message ID → index (or scroll offset); if paged, resolve via storage; use search result IDs as jump targets. (5) **Edge cases:** Deleted/rewound target → "Message not found"; target in unloaded older region → trigger load older, then scroll.

(4) **Data:** Store match ranges (start, end offset) per message; compute on search or when message enters view; cache by (message_id, query); thread search query available to chat view; clear on search clear or thread change.

Keep the **currently streaming** message in the visible window (e.g. scroll to bottom when streaming starts, or ensure the last item is always in the overscan). When user has scrolled up during stream, do not auto-scroll; only auto-scroll when already at bottom.

No hard limit for persistence. For display, virtualization and optional "load older" keep the UI bounded. Document that threads with 10k+ messages may need pagination or load-older in addition to virtualization.
- **Provider dropdown** — lists enabled provider entries from the same account-bound Provider -> models registry as the chat provider dropdown. Label: "Provider".

4. **First eligible provider entry + model** — if the primary chat provider/model is also unset, select the first eligible account-bound provider entry and model from the Provider -> models registry after readiness, capability, and policy filtering.
- Given the same app settings state, the same provider and model are always selected (no randomness, no environment-dependent branching).
Auditor loop selections are stored in **app settings** only. They are not stored in project artifacts, not emitted to seglog as project data, and not included in project exports.
| `model_roles.auditor.provider` | Provider for the Auditor validation loop |
| `model_roles.auditor.model` | Model for the Auditor validation loop |
| 1 | Settings changes take effect on the **next** validation sweep run — not mid-sweep. A sweep in progress uses the provider/model that was active when it started. |

| 2 | When a saved provider is no longer available (platform uninstalled or disabled), Puppet Master falls back to the deterministic default (§26.4) and displays a warning: *"Auditor validation provider [name] is unavailable; using Auditor Model default."* |

| 7 | For each emitted Auditor cycle report, `.provider` and `.model` values match the resolved Auditor loop provider/model from sweep start; legacy `validation_pass_report` mirrors follow the same rule (see `Plans/Project_Output_Artifacts.md §10.2`). |
- **hybrid:** auto selects by default, but the user may temporarily or persistently override it.

Chat selection consumes the eligibility rules in `Plans/Personas.md`: `assistant` is the default direct-chat Persona; `explorer` and `bash` are subagent-only and cannot be selected as the direct chat Persona; `teacher` is direct-chat eligible but not a subagent Persona.

Chat MUST NOT invent assistant-local substitutes: `requested_persona_id` and `effective_persona_id` normalize to `requested_persona` and `effective_persona`; `active_model` and `actual_model` normalize to `effective_model`;

- requested_persona_id
- effective_persona_id
- `Run that with Bash`

- `for this`, `for this answer`, `right now` -> turn scope,
- `from now on`, `in this chat`, `for this session` -> session scope.

Subagent-only requests such as `Ask Explorer` or `Run that with Bash` create or route a child run when the surrounding task permits delegation; they do not switch the direct chat Persona. If the user asks to make a subagent-only Persona the direct chat Persona, chat must explain the eligibility constraint and offer the closest valid route.

- **Natural-language request:** chat must ask for clarification (for example, nearest matches or a prompt to pick a Persona) before starting a run; it must not silently pretend a request resolved when it did not.
- **Persisted unresolved reference:** if a stored/manual/auto Persona reference reaches runtime and remains unresolved, the fallback contract in `Plans/Personas.md` §2.3 applies, and chat must surface that the run is proceeding without Persona context.
- and a way to lock/unlock the current Persona.

- Inline visualizer iframes MUST use an explicit `sandbox` attribute token set. The sandbox policy is closed by default: MVP uses `sandbox="allow-scripts"` so the module can execute its bundled code, and the exact minimum attribute is `sandbox='allow-scripts'`. `allow-same-origin`, `allow-forms`, `allow-popups`, and `allow-top-navigation` are explicitly DENIED; the iframe stays isolated from the PM origin, and all cross-boundary communication uses the `postMessage` bridge as the only allowed bridge.

- Non-iframe Markdown, Mermaid, HTML, and SVG rendering uses the rendering contract here until a dedicated `Plans/security-sanitization.md` owner exists; `/security-sanitization.md` is lineage for that proposed split, not the current owner. The baseline sanitizer is the standard HTML5 safe subset per DOMPurify `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TAGS` plus approved URL-bearing attributes only; raw `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, and `<style>` with external URL references are denied in message-flow rendering.

- The inline visualizer host bridge exposes only async-safe calls: `sendPrompt(text: string): void`, `openLink(url: string, target?: "_blank" | "_self"): void`, `copyToClipboard(text: string): Promise<boolean>`, and `requestResize(width?: number, height?: number): void`. `openLink` treats `_blank` as a new tab and blocks `_self` navigation inside the sandbox; `requestResize` is advisory and the host may constrain it. For question-flow embedded visual modules, the host omits `sendPrompt` from the bridge and exposes only the narrowed PM-managed question-draft bridge, so visuals cannot bypass PM draft state by queueing chat messages.

- Bridge calls preserve exact host semantics: `sendPrompt(text)` queues into the active thread composer outside question-flow contexts; dual-context enforcement means that if a questionnaire is active when `sendPrompt` is called from within a visualizer, the text is routed as a question answer rather than a new chat message, and if no questionnaire is active it is routed as a new chat input. Question-flow embedded visuals do not receive `sendPrompt` and write draft answers only through the narrowed question bridge, so the visualizer cannot bypass the question flow; `openLink(url)` routes through `cmd.browser.open_detached_preview` or the system browser when external; theme injection pushes the CSS custom property bundle on mount and theme change; auto-height/resize reporting sends `{ height: px }` to the host, which adjusts the visual card height within host constraints.

- The visualizer is a general-purpose surface for user-requested or clearly helpful quizzes, interactive visualizations, and other artifacts; it may use third-party script `/library` code inside the sandbox only when policy allows, with bundled, version-pinned, and integrity-recorded code. Arbitrary external network loads are denied; the visualizer is not limited to `/questions`, and it is not an accessibility-only fallback path.

Required requested/effective fields are:
- `requested_mode_overlay`
- `effective_mode_overlay`
- `requested_runtime_mode`
- `effective_runtime_mode`
- `requested_plan_thoroughness`
- `effective_plan_thoroughness`
- `selection_source`
- `selection_reason`
- `override_scope`

- `requested_mode_overlay` and `effective_mode_overlay` are closed to `none`, `plan`, `deep_plan`, `debug`, `interview`, `brainstorm`, and `crew`
- `requested_runtime_mode` and `effective_runtime_mode` are closed to the canonical runtime postures from `Plans/Run_Modes.md`
- `deep_plan` MUST survive normalization through the overlay fields and MUST NOT be discarded from historical/runtime records simply because the runtime posture is planning
